title.zh: 卷八十四 志第六十 河渠二
title.raw: 卷八十四 志第六十 河渠二 Volume 84 Treatises 60: Rivers and Canals 2

sentences.zh: 黃河下

translations.literal: Yellow River, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River (Continued)

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年，河決房村，築堤□子頭至秦溝口。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Wanli reign, the river breached at Fangcun, and embankments were built from Yaozitou to Qingoukou.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 1, the Yellow River broke through at Fangcun; dikes were then raised from Yaozitou to Qingoukou.

sentences.zh: 明年，給事中鄭嶽言：「運道自茶城至淮安五百餘里，自嘉靖四十四年河水大發，淮口出水之際，海沙漸淤，今且高與山等。

translations.literal: The next year, the Supervising Secretary Zheng Yue said: "The transport route from Chacheng to Huai'an stretches more than five hundred li. Since the great flood of the forty-fourth year of the Jiajing reign, as the Huai River mouth discharged, sea sand has gradually silted up, and now it stands as high as mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Supervising Secretary Zheng Yue memorialized: "The grain route from Chacheng to Huai'an runs more than five hundred li. Ever since the great flood of Jiajing 44, sand from the sea has piled up where the Huai empties into the ocean until it now rises level with the hills.

sentences.zh: 自淮而上，河流不迅，泥水愈淤。

translations.literal: Upstream from the Huai, the river current is not swift, and muddy water silts up all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Above the Huai junction the current slackened, and silt-laden water accumulated ever faster.

sentences.zh: 於是邳州淺，房村決，呂、梁二洪平，茶城倒流，皆坐此也。

translations.literal: Thus the channel at Pizhou grew shallow, Fangcun breached, the Lu and Liang rapids were levelled, and Chacheng saw reverse flow—all owing to this.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the reach at Pizhou shoaled, Fangcun broke, the Lu and Liang shoals flattened out, and the current at Chacheng reversed—all consequences of this siltation.

sentences.zh: 今不治海口之沙，乃日築徐、沛間堤岸，桃、宿而下，聽其所之。

translations.literal: Now, without dredging the sand at the river mouth, they daily build dikes between Xu and Pei, and from Taoyuan and Suxian downstream, letting the river go where it will.
translations.idiomatic: Instead of clearing sand at the estuary, officials keep raising dikes between Xu and Pei and, from Taoyuan and Suxian downstream, simply let the river wander where it pleases.

sentences.zh: 民之為魚，未有已時也。

translations.literal: The people becoming fish in the water will never cease.
translations.idiomatic: The common people will never cease to be drowned like fish in a net.

sentences.zh: 」因獻宋李公義、王令圖浚川爬法。

translations.literal: " He thereupon presented the dredging and raking methods of Li Gongyi and Wang Ling of the Song dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted the river-dredging and rake-scoop methods devised by Li Gongyi and Wang Ling of the Song.

sentences.zh: 命河臣勘奏，從其所言。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the river officials to investigate and report, and followed what they said.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the river commissioners to survey the site and report back, and their recommendations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 而是年秋，淮、河並溢。

translations.literal: But that autumn, both the Huai and the Yellow River overflowed together.
translations.idiomatic: Yet that same autumn both the Huai and the Yellow River burst their banks together.

sentences.zh: 明年八月河決碭山及邵家口、曹家莊、韓登家口而北，淮亦決高家堰而東，徐、邳、淮南北漂沒千里。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year the river breached at Dangshan and at Shaojiakou, Caojiazhuang, and Handengjiakou to the north; the Huai also breached the Gaojia Weir to the east, and for a thousand li north and south of Xu, Pi, and Huai the land was swept away and submerged.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the eighth month, the Yellow River broke northward at Dangshan, Shaojiakou, Caojiazhuang, and Handengjiakou, while the Huai burst eastward through the Gaojia Weir; for a thousand li around Xu, Pi, and the Huai region, fields and settlements were washed away.

sentences.zh: 自此桃、清上下河道淤塞，漕艘梗阻者數年，淮、揚多水患矣。

translations.literal: From this time the channels above and below Taoyuan and Qinghe silted up, grain barges were blocked for several years, and Huai and Yang suffered many flood disasters.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the waterways above and below Taoyuan and Qinghe choked with silt; grain transport was obstructed for years, and the Huai-Yang region suffered repeated floods.

sentences.zh: 總河都御史傅希摯改築碭山月堤，暫留三口為泄水之路。

translations.literal: The Grand Coordinator for Rivers, Fu Xizhi, rebuilt the crescent dike at Dangshan and temporarily left three openings as paths for discharging water.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator for Rivers Fu Xizhi rebuilt the crescent dike at Dangshan, leaving three temporary outlets to release floodwater.

sentences.zh: 其冬，並塞之。

translations.literal: That winter, all were closed up.
translations.idiomatic: That winter all three outlets were sealed shut.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，督漕侍郎吳桂芒言：「淮、揚洪潦奔沖，蓋緣海賓汊港久堙，入海止雲梯一徑，致海擁橫沙，河流泛溢，而鹽、安、高、寶不可收拾。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, the Vice Minister in charge of grain transport, Wu Guifang, said: "The raging floods in Huai and Yang rush and batter because the sea-side branching channels have long been blocked; there is only the single route at Yunti into the sea, causing the sea to push up cross-sands, the river to overflow, and Yan, An, Gao, and Bao to become beyond recovery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 4, Vice Minister of Grain Transport Wu Guifang memorialized: "The violent floods in the Huai-Yang region stem from the long-blocked estuary channels along the coast: only the Yunti Pass offers a path to the sea. The sea has piled sand across the mouth, the river spills over, and the districts of Yan, An, Gao, and Bao are beyond control.

sentences.zh: 國家轉運，惟知急漕，而不暇急漕，而不暇急民，故朝廷設官，亦主治河，而不知治海。

translations.literal: In the state's transport of grain, they only know to hurry the tribute transport, but have no time to hurry the tribute transport, and have no time to hurry relief for the people; therefore the court appoints officials mainly to govern the river, but does not know to govern the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In running the grain tribute the state knows only to rush the barges along, with no time to address the rivers and no time to relieve the people. The court appoints officials chiefly to manage the Yellow River, yet pays no heed to the sea outlet.

sentences.zh: 請設水利僉事一員，專疏海道，審度地利，如草灣及老黃河皆可趨海，何必專事雲梯哉？

translations.literal: I request that one Assistant Commissioner for Water Works be appointed to specialize in clearing the sea route, assess the terrain, and recognize that Caowan and the Old Yellow River can both reach the sea—why must we rely on Yunti alone?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that an Assistant Commissioner for Water Works be appointed to open sea routes, survey the terrain, and recognize that both Caowan and the Old Yellow River can reach the sea. Why fixate on Yunti alone?

sentences.zh: 」帝優詔報可。

translations.literal: " The emperor replied with an gracious edict approving the request.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor issued a gracious edict approving the proposal.

sentences.zh: 桂芳復言：「黃水抵清河與淮合流，經清江浦外河，東至草灣，又折而西南，過淮安、新城外河，轉入安東縣前，直下雲梯關入海。

translations.literal: Guifang further said: "Yellow River water reaches Qinghe and joins the Huai, passes the outer channel at Qingjiangpu, goes east to Caowan, then turns southwest, passes the outer channels of Huai'an and Xincheng, turns before Andong County, and runs straight down through Yunti Pass into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Guifang added: "Yellow River water reaches Qinghe, merges with the Huai, runs through the outer channel at Qingjiangpu east to Caowan, then bends southwest past the outer channels of Huai'an and Xincheng, turns before Andong County, and pours straight through Yunti Pass into the sea.

sentences.zh: 近年關口多壅，河流日淺，惟草灣地低下，黃河沖決，駸駸欲奪安東入海，以縣治所關，屢決屢塞。

translations.literal: In recent years the pass has often silted up and the river grows shallower by the day. Only Caowan lies low; the Yellow River breaks through and presses ever closer to seize Andong and enter the sea. Because the county seat is involved, it has been breached and blocked again and again.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the pass has repeatedly choked and the channel grows shallower. Caowan sits lower than the surrounding land, and the Yellow River keeps breaking through, pressing to cut off Andong and reach the sea. Because the county seat stands in the way, each breach has been plugged again and again.

sentences.zh: 去歲，草灣迤東自決一口，宜於決口之西開挑新口，以迎埽灣之溜，而於金城至五港岸築堤束水。

translations.literal: Last year Caowan breached by itself to the east. A new opening should be cut west of the breach to receive the current from Saowan, and dikes should be built from Jincheng to the Wugang shore to confine the water.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Caowan broke open on its own to the east. We should cut a new outlet west of the breach to catch the current from Saowan, and build dikes from Jincheng to the Wugang shore to channel the water.

sentences.zh: 語云：「救一路哭，不當復計一家哭。

translations.literal: A saying goes: "When saving those weeping along the road, one should not again count those weeping in a single household.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, "When an entire road is in mourning, one cannot stop to weigh the grief of a single household.

sentences.zh: 」今淮、揚、鳳、泗、邳、徐不啻一路矣。

translations.literal: " Now Huai, Yang, Feng, Si, Pi, and Xu are more than one road in distress.
translations.idiomatic: " Today the regions of Huai, Yang, Feng, Si, Pi, and Xu are suffering on far more than one road.

sentences.zh: 安東自眾流匯圍，只文廟、縣署僅存椽瓦，其勢垂陷，不如委之，以拯全淮。

translations.literal: Andong is already encircled by converging streams; only the Confucian temple and county yamen still have rafters and tiles left, and it is on the verge of collapse. It would be better to abandon it to save the whole Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: Andong is already ringed by converging currents; only the Confucian temple and county offices still have roof timbers standing, and the town is about to sink. Better to yield the county than fail to save the entire Huai basin.

sentences.zh: 」帝不欲棄安東，而命開草灣如所請。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not wish to abandon Andong, but ordered Caowan opened as requested.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused to abandon Andong, but ordered Caowan opened as Guifang had proposed.

sentences.zh: 八月，工竣，長萬一千一百餘丈，塞決口二十二，役夫四萬四千。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the work was completed: more than eleven thousand one hundred zhang in length, twenty-two breaches closed, and forty-four thousand laborers employed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the project was finished—more than 11,100 zhang of channel, twenty-two breaches sealed, and 44,000 laborers mobilized.

sentences.zh: 帝以海口開浚，水患漸平，賚桂芳等有差。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the river mouth had been opened and dredged and flood disasters were gradually easing, rewarded Guifang and others in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Because the estuary had been opened and floods were subsiding, the emperor granted Guifang and his colleagues graded rewards.

sentences.zh: 未幾，河決韋家樓，又決沛縣縷水堤，豐、曹二縣長堤，豐、沛、徐州、睢甯、金鄉、魚臺、單、曹田廬漂溺無算，河流齧宿遷城。

translations.literal: Before long the river breached at Weijialou, then broke the Lüshui dike in Pei County and the long dikes of Feng and Cao counties. In Feng, Pei, Xuzhou, Suining, Jinxiang, Yutai, Shan, and Cao, fields and dwellings were swept away beyond count, and the river gnawed at Suqian city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the river broke at Weijialou, then burst the Lüshui dike in Pei County and the long dikes of Feng and Cao. Across Feng, Pei, Xuzhou, Suining, Jinxiang, Yutai, Shan, and Cao, countless farms and homes were inundated, and the current began eating away at Suqian city.

sentences.zh: 帝從桂芳請，遷縣治、築土城避之。

translations.literal: The emperor, following Guifang's request, moved the county seat and built an earthen wall to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: At Guifang's urging the emperor relocated the county seat and built an earthen fortification to escape the flood.

sentences.zh: 於是御史陳世寶請復老黃河故道，言：「河自桃源三義鎮歷清河縣北，至大河口會淮入海。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Censor Chen Shibao requested restoration of the Old Yellow River's former course, saying: "The river from Sanyizhen in Taoyuan passed north of Qinghe County to Dahekou, where it joined the Huai and entered the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Shibao then petitioned to restore the Old Yellow River's former channel, stating: "The river once ran from Sanyizhen in Taoyuan north of Qinghe County to Dahekou, where it met the Huai and reached the sea.

sentences.zh: 運道自淮安天妃廟亂淮而下，十里至大河口，從三義鎮出口向桃源大河而去，凡七十餘里，是為老黃河。

translations.literal: The transport route from the Tianfei Temple in Huai'an followed the Huai downstream for ten li to Dahekou, then exited at Sanyizhen toward the great river at Taoyuan—a total of more than seventy li—this being the Old Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The grain route ran from the Tianfei Temple in Huai'an down the Huai for ten li to Dahekou, then left through Sanyizhen toward Taoyuan's main channel—a stretch of more than seventy li known as the Old Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 至嘉靖初，三義鎮口淤，而黃河改趨清河縣南與淮會，自此運道不由大河口而徑由清河北上矣。

translations.literal: By the early Jiajing reign Sanyizhen mouth silted up, and the Yellow River shifted to run south of Qinghe County to meet the Huai; from then the transport route no longer passed Dahekou but went directly north along the Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: By the early Jiajing period the mouth at Sanyizhen had silted shut and the Yellow River swung south of Qinghe to join the Huai. Thereafter the grain route bypassed Dahekou and ran straight north along the Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 近者，崔鎮屢決，河勢漸趨故道。

translations.literal: Recently Cuizhen has breached repeatedly, and the river's course is gradually returning to the old channel.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Cuizhen has broken repeatedly, and the river is gradually shifting back toward its old course.

sentences.zh: 若仍開三義鎮口引河入清河北，或令出大河口與淮流合，或從清河西別開一河，引淮出河上游，則運道無恐，而淮、泗之水不為黃流所漲。

translations.literal: If Sanyizhen mouth is reopened to lead the river north of Qinghe, or it is made to exit at Dahekou and merge with the Huai current, or a separate channel is cut west of Qinghe to draw the Huai out upstream of the river, then the transport route need not fear disaster and the waters of Huai and Si will not be swollen by the Yellow current.
translations.idiomatic: If we reopen Sanyizhen to bring the river north of Qinghe, or send it out at Dahekou to merge with the Huai, or cut a new channel west of Qinghe to draw the Huai above the junction, the grain route would be secure and the Huai and Si would no longer be swelled by Yellow River water.

sentences.zh: 」部覆允行。

translations.literal: " The ministry replied approving implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry approved the plan for implementation.

sentences.zh: 桂芳言：「淮水向經清河會黃河趨海。

translations.literal: Guifang said: "Huai water formerly passed through Qinghe to meet the Yellow River and reach the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Guifang reported: "Huai water used to pass through Qinghe, join the Yellow River, and reach the sea.

sentences.zh: 自去秋河決崔鎮，清江正河淤澱，淮口梗塞。

translations.literal: Since last autumn, when the river breached at Cuizhen, the main channel at Qingjiang silted up and the Huai mouth was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Since the breach at Cuizhen last autumn, the main channel at Qingjiang has silted up and the Huai mouth is choked.

sentences.zh: 於是淮弱河強，不能奪草灣入海之途，而全淮南徙，橫灌山陽、高、寶間，向來湖水不逾五尺，堤僅七尺，今堤加丈二，而水更過之。

translations.literal: Thus the Huai was weak and the river strong; it could not seize Caowan's path to the sea, and the whole Huai shifted south, flooding across Shanyang, Gao, and Bao. Formerly lake water did not exceed five chi and dikes were only seven chi; now the dikes have been raised by one zhang and two chi, yet the water still surpasses them.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai grew weak while the Yellow River grew strong, unable to hold Caowan's route to the sea. The entire Huai shifted south and poured across Shanyang, Gao, and Bao. Lake levels once stayed below five chi and dikes stood only seven chi high; though dikes have now been raised by twelve chi, the water still overtops them.

sentences.zh: 宜急護湖堤以殺水勢。

translations.literal: Lake dikes should urgently be protected to reduce the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: Lake dikes must be reinforced at once to check the flood.

sentences.zh: 」部議以為必淮有所歸，而後堤可保，請令桂芳等熟計。

translations.literal: " The ministry judged that the Huai must have somewhere to go before the dikes can be secured, and requested that Guifang and others deliberate carefully.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry held that the Huai must have an outlet before the dikes can hold, and asked Guifang and his colleagues to plan accordingly.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 開河、護堤二說未定，而河復決崔鎮，宿、沛、清、桃兩岸多壞，黃河日淤墊，淮水為河所迫，徙而南，時五年八月也。

translations.literal: The two proposals—to open a channel and to protect dikes—had not been settled when the river again breached at Cuizhen. Both banks at Su, Pei, Qing, and Tao suffered much damage; the Yellow River silted up daily, and Huai water, pressed by the river, shifted south. This was in the eighth month of the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: Before the rival plans to open a channel or strengthen dikes could be settled, the river broke again at Cuizhen. Both banks from Su and Pei to Qing and Tao were badly damaged; the Yellow River rose with silt day by day, and the Huai, forced aside, shifted south. This occurred in the eighth month of year 5.

sentences.zh: 希摯議塞決口，束水歸漕。

translations.literal: Xizhi proposed closing the breach and confining the water to return to the transport channel.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi urged sealing the breach and channeling the water back into the grain route.

sentences.zh: 桂芳欲沖刷成河，以為老黃河入海之路。

translations.literal: Guifang wished to scour out a channel to serve as the Old Yellow River's path to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Guifang wanted to scour open a channel to restore the Old Yellow River's route to the sea.

sentences.zh: 帝令急塞決口，而俟水勢稍定，乃從桂芳言。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the breach closed urgently, and after the water's force had settled somewhat, then followed Guifang's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the breach sealed at once, and once the flood had subsided somewhat, adopted Guifang's plan.

sentences.zh: 時給事中湯聘尹議導淮入江以避黃，會桂芳言：「黃水向老黃河故道而去，下奔如駛，淮遂乘虛湧入清口故道，淮、揚水勢漸消。

translations.literal: At the time the Supervising Secretary Tang Pinyin proposed diverting the Huai into the Yangtze to avoid the Yellow River. Just then Guifang said: "Yellow River water is heading down the Old Yellow River's former course, rushing downstream like a galloping horse; the Huai has seized the opening and surged into the old channel at Qingkou, and the flood in Huai and Yang is gradually subsiding.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Tang Pinyin had proposed diverting the Huai into the Yangtze to escape the Yellow River. Guifang reported at the same time: "Yellow River water is racing down the Old Yellow River's former course; the Huai has rushed into the old channel at Qingkou, and flooding in the Huai-Yang region is easing.

sentences.zh: 」部議行勘，以河、淮既合，乃寢其議。

translations.literal: " The ministry ordered an investigation, but because the Yellow River and Huai had already joined, the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry ordered a survey, but because the Yellow River and Huai had already merged, Tang's proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 管理南河工部郎中施天麟言：

translations.literal: Shi Tianlin, Director in the Ministry of Works managing southern river works, said:
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianlin, Director in the Ministry of Works in charge of southern river works, memorialized:

sentences.zh: 「淮、泗之水不下清口而下山陽，從黃浦口入海。

translations.literal: "The waters of Huai and Si should not descend below Qingkou and down through Shanyang to enter the sea at Huangpukou.
translations.idiomatic: "The Huai and Si ought to run below Qingkou through Shanyang and reach the sea at Huangpukou.

sentences.zh: 浦口不能盡泄，浸淫高、寶邵伯諸湖，而湖堤盡沒，則以淮、泗本不入湖，而今入湖故也。

translations.literal: Pukou cannot discharge it all; it spreads into the lakes of Gao, Bao, and Shaobo, and the lake dikes are wholly submerged—because Huai and Si water originally did not enter the lakes, but now it does.
translations.idiomatic: Huangpukou cannot release it all, so the water spreads into the Gao, Bao, and Shaobo lakes and overtops their dikes—because Huai and Si water never used to enter those lakes, but now it does.

sentences.zh: 淮、泗之入湖者，又緣清口向未淤塞，而今淤塞故也。

translations.literal: That Huai and Si water enters the lakes is further because Qingkou was formerly not silted up, but now it is.
translations.idiomatic: The reason Huai and Si water now backs into the lakes is that Qingkou, once open, has silted shut.

sentences.zh: 清口之淤塞者，又緣黃河淤塞日高，淮水不得不讓河而南徙也。

translations.literal: Qingkou's silting up, in turn, is because the Yellow River silts up daily and grows higher, and Huai water has no choice but to yield to the river and shift south.
translations.idiomatic: Qingkou choked because the Yellow River silts higher each day, forcing the Huai to give way and shift south.

sentences.zh: 蓋淮水並力敵黃，勝負或亦相半，自高家堰廢壞，而清口內通濟橋、硃家等口淮水內灌，於是淮、泗之力分，而黃河得以全力制其敝，此清口所以獨淤於今歲也。

translations.literal: Huai water, combining its strength, could match the Yellow River and victory or defeat might be even; but since the Gaojia Weir fell into ruin, Huai water poured inward through Tongji Bridge, Zhujia, and other openings at Qingkou. Thereupon the force of Huai and Si was divided, and the Yellow River could bring its full strength to exploit their weakness—this is why Qingkou alone silted up this year.
translations.idiomatic: Combined, Huai water could once contend evenly with the Yellow River, but after the Gaojia Weir collapsed, the Huai poured inland through Tongji Bridge, Zhujia, and other openings at Qingkou. The Huai and Si were split in force, and the Yellow River brought its full weight against them—that is why Qingkou alone silted up this year.

sentences.zh: 下流既淤，則上流不得不決。

translations.literal: When the lower reach is silted, the upper reach must inevitably breach.
translations.idiomatic: When the lower course silts up, the upper course must break out.

sentences.zh: 每歲糧艘以四五月畢運，而堤以六七月壞。

translations.literal: Each year grain barges finish transport in the fourth and fifth months, but dikes break in the sixth and seventh months.
translations.idiomatic: Every year the grain fleet finishes in the fourth and fifth months, yet the dikes fail in the sixth and seventh.

sentences.zh: 水發之時不能為力，水落之後方圖堵塞。

translations.literal: When the water rises they cannot act effectively; only after it falls do they plan to block the breaches.
translations.idiomatic: When floods peak nothing effective can be done; repairs begin only after the water drops.

sentences.zh: 甫及春初，運事又迫，僅完堤工，於河身無與。

translations.literal: Hardly has early spring arrived when transport duties press again; they barely finish dike work and do nothing for the river channel itself.
translations.idiomatic: Barely has early spring arrived when the grain season presses again; workers finish the dikes but leave the riverbed untouched.

sentences.zh: 河身不挑則來年益高。

translations.literal: If the river channel is not dredged, next year it will grow higher still.
translations.idiomatic: Without dredging the channel, the riverbed will rise even higher the following year.

sentences.zh: 上流之決，必及於徐、呂，而不止於邳、遷；

translations.literal: Breaches in the upper reach will surely reach Xu and Lü, and not stop at Pi and Qian;
translations.idiomatic: Breaches upstream will reach Xu and Lü, not stop at Pi and Suqian alone;

sentences.zh: 下流之涸，將盡乎邳、遷，而不止於清、桃。

translations.literal: drying in the lower reach will extend through Pi and Qian, and not stop at Qing and Tao.
translations.idiomatic: and drying downstream will spread through Pi and Suqian, not halt at Qing and Tao alone.

sentences.zh: 須不惜一年糧運，不惜數萬帑藏，開挑正河，寬限責成，乃為一勞永逸。

translations.literal: We must not spare one year's grain transport, must not spare tens of thousands from the treasury, but open and dredge the main channel with ample time for completion—only then will there be lasting relief from a single effort.
translations.idiomatic: We must be willing to sacrifice one year's grain transport and spend tens of thousands from the treasury to dredge the main channel, with a generous deadline for completion—that alone would bring lasting relief.

sentences.zh: 至高家堰、硃家等口，宜及時築塞，使淮、泗並力足以敵黃，則淮水之故道可復，高、寶之大患可減。

translations.literal: As for the Gaojia Weir, Zhujia, and other openings, they should be blocked in good time so that Huai and Si combined have strength enough to match the Yellow River; then the Huai's old course can be restored and the great disaster in Gao and Bao can be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaojia Weir, Zhujia, and similar openings should be sealed promptly so the Huai and Si together can stand against the Yellow River; then the Huai's old course can be restored and the worst floods in Gao and Bao eased.

sentences.zh: 若興、鹽海口堙塞，亦宜大加疏浚。

translations.literal: If the river mouths at Xing and Yan are blocked, they too should be heavily dredged.
translations.idiomatic: If the estuaries at Xing and Yan are choked, they too require major dredging.

sentences.zh: 而湖堤多建減水大閘，堤下多開支河。

translations.literal: On the lake dikes many flood-release sluices should be built, and below the dikes many branch channels opened.
translations.idiomatic: Lake dikes should be fitted with major flood-release gates, and branch channels opened below them.

sentences.zh: 要未有不先黃河而可以治淮，亦未有不疏通淮水而可以固堤者也。

translations.literal: In sum, there is no way to govern the Huai without first dealing with the Yellow River, and no way to secure dikes without clearing the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In short, the Huai cannot be managed without first controlling the Yellow River, nor can dikes hold without freeing the Huai's course.

sentences.zh: 」事下河漕諸臣會議。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the river and grain transport officials for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was sent to the river and grain transport officials for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 淮之出清口也，以黃水由老黃河奔注，而老黃河久淤，未幾復塞，淮水仍漲溢。

translations.literal: When the Huai exited at Qingkou, Yellow River water rushed in through the Old Yellow River; but the Old Yellow River had long been silted up and soon blocked again, and Huai water still rose and overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai had been exiting at Qingkou while Yellow River water poured in through the Old Yellow River, but that channel had long been silted and soon blocked again, and Huai water continued to rise and spill over.

sentences.zh: 給事中劉鉉請亟開通海口，而簡大臣會同河漕諸臣往治。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary Liu Xuan requested that the river mouth be opened urgently and that a senior minister be selected to go with the river and grain transport officials to manage it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Xuan urged that the estuary be opened at once and that a senior minister be dispatched with the river and grain transport officials to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 乃命桂芳為工部尚書兼理河漕，而裁總河都御史官。

translations.literal: Guifang was then appointed Minister of Works with concurrent charge of river and grain transport, and the post of Grand Coordinator for Rivers was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Guifang was appointed Minister of Works with concurrent authority over river and grain transport, and the separate Grand Coordinator for Rivers post was abolished.

sentences.zh: 桂芳甫受命而卒。

translations.literal: Guifang had barely taken office when he died.
translations.idiomatic: Guifang died soon after taking up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，潘季馴代。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year, Pan Jixun replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year 6, Pan Jixun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 時給事中李淶請多浚海口，以導眾水之歸。

translations.literal: At the time the Supervising Secretary Li Lai requested extensive dredging of the river mouth to guide the convergence of all waters.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Lai petitioned for extensive dredging of the estuary to channel all the waters to the sea.

sentences.zh: 給事中王道成則請塞崔鎮決口，築桃、宿長堤，修理高家堰，開復老黃河。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary Wang Daocheng, for his part, requested closing the breach at Cuizhen, building long dikes at Tao and Su, repairing the Gaojia Weir, and reopening the Old Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wang Daocheng proposed sealing the breach at Cuizhen, building long dikes at Tao and Su, repairing the Gaojia Weir, and restoring the Old Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 並下河臣議。

translations.literal: Both proposals were sent down to the river officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were referred to the river commissioners for review.

sentences.zh: 季馴與督漕侍郎江一麟相度水勢，言：

translations.literal: Jixun and the Vice Minister in charge of grain transport, Jiang Yilin, surveyed the water conditions and said:
translations.idiomatic: Jixun and Vice Minister of Grain Transport Jiang Yilin surveyed the water conditions and reported:

sentences.zh: 「海口自雲梯關四套以下，闊七八里至十餘里，深三四丈。

translations.literal: "From Yunti Pass downstream through the four sets of channels, the width is seven or eight li to more than ten li, and the depth three or four zhang.
translations.idiomatic: "From Yunti Pass downstream through the four channel sets, the estuary spans seven or eight li to more than ten li wide and runs three or four zhang deep.

sentences.zh: 欲別議開鑿，必須深闊相類，方可注放，工力甚難。

translations.literal: If one wishes to propose separate excavation, depth and width must be comparable before water can be discharged—an extremely difficult labor.
translations.idiomatic: Any new cut would have to match that depth and width before it could carry the flow—an almost impossible task.

sentences.zh: 且未至海口，乾地猶可施工，其將入海之地，潮汐往來，與舊口等耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, before reaching the river mouth dry land still permits construction; but where it enters the sea, the tides ebb and flow, making it the same as the old mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Before the estuary, work can still proceed on dry ground; but at the sea itself the tides surge back and forth, making any new mouth no different from the old one.

sentences.zh: 舊口皆系積沙，人力雖不可浚，水力自能沖刷，海無可浚之理。

translations.literal: The old mouths are all accumulated sand; human power cannot dredge them, but water power can scour them by itself—there is no principle by which the sea can be dredged.
translations.idiomatic: The old mouths are packed with sand that human labor cannot remove, but the current itself can scour them away—the sea cannot be dredged by hand.

sentences.zh: 惟當導河歸海，則以水治水，即浚海之策也。

translations.literal: One need only guide the river back to the sea; using water to govern water is precisely the strategy for dredging the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The answer is to guide the river back to the sea—using water to master water is itself the way to clear the estuary.

sentences.zh: 河亦非可以人力導，惟當繕治堤防，俾無旁決，則水由地中，沙隨水去，即導河之策也。

translations.literal: The river likewise cannot be guided by human power; one need only repair the dikes so there are no side breaches, and water will run through the channel while sand goes with the water—this is the strategy for guiding the river.
translations.idiomatic: Nor can the river be steered by human force alone; repair the dikes to prevent side breaches, let water run in its bed and sand wash away with it—that is how to guide the river.

sentences.zh: 頻年以來，日以繕堤為事，顧卑薄而不能支，迫近而不能容，雜以浮沙而不能久。

translations.literal: Year after year the daily task has been repairing dikes—yet they are too low and thin to bear the strain, too close to the river to hold the water, and mixed with loose sand so they cannot last.
translations.idiomatic: For years the daily work has been dike repair—yet the dikes are too low and thin to bear the strain, too close to the channel to hold the water, and built with loose sand so they cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 是以河決崔鎮，水多北潰，為無堤也。

translations.literal: Thus when the river breached at Cuizhen, much water burst northward—for lack of dikes.
translations.idiomatic: That is why when the river broke at Cuizhen, water poured north—for lack of dikes.

sentences.zh: 淮決高家堰、黃浦口，水多東潰，堤弗固也。

translations.literal: When the Huai breached the Gaojia Weir and Huangpukou, much water burst eastward—the dikes were not solid.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai broke through the Gaojia Weir and Huangpukou, water poured eastward—the dikes were not strong enough.

sentences.zh: 不咎制之未備，而咎築堤為下策，豈通論哉！

translations.literal: To blame not the incompleteness of control measures but dike-building as a poor strategy—is this sound reasoning?
translations.idiomatic: To fault dike-building as a poor strategy rather than the failure to build them properly—is that sound reasoning?

sentences.zh: 上流既旁潰，又岐下流而分之，其趨雲梯入海口者，譬猶強弩之末耳。

translations.literal: The upper reach having already burst sideways, and the lower reach further split and divided, what reaches Yunti and enters the sea is like the last force of a strong crossbow.
translations.idiomatic: With the upper course already spilling sideways and the lower course split into branches, what reaches Yunti and the sea is like the spent bolt of a crossbow.

sentences.zh: 水勢益分則力益弱，安能導積沙以注海？

translations.literal: As the water's force is further divided its power grows weaker—how can it scour accumulated sand and pour into the sea?
translations.idiomatic: The more the current is divided, the weaker it grows—how can it scour sand and reach the sea?

sentences.zh: 故今日浚海急務，必先塞決以導河，尤當固堤以杜決，而欲堤之不決，必真土而勿雜浮沙，高厚而勿惜鉅費，讓遠而勿與爭地，則堤乃可固也。

translations.literal: Therefore today's urgent task for dredging the sea must first seal breaches to guide the river, and above all solidify dikes to prevent breaches. For dikes not to break, one must use true earth and not mix in loose sand, build high and thick and not spare great expense, set them far back and not contest land with the river—then dikes can be made solid.
translations.idiomatic: Today's urgent work is to seal breaches to guide the river and, above all, strengthen dikes to prevent new breaks. Dikes will hold only if built of solid earth without loose sand, raised high and thick at whatever cost, and set far back from the channel rather than hugging the bank—then they can endure.

sentences.zh: 沿河堤固，而崔鎮口塞，則黃不旁決而沖漕力專。

translations.literal: When dikes along the river are solid and the opening at Cuizhen is closed, the Yellow River will not burst sideways and its force to scour the transport channel will be concentrated.
translations.idiomatic: With solid dikes along the river and Cuizhen sealed, the Yellow River will not spill sideways and its scouring force will concentrate on the grain channel.

sentences.zh: 高家堰築，硃家口塞，則淮不旁決而會黃力專。

translations.literal: When the Gaojia Weir is built and Zhujiakou is closed, the Huai will not burst sideways and its force to meet the Yellow River will be concentrated.
translations.idiomatic: With the Gaojia Weir rebuilt and Zhujiakou sealed, the Huai will not spill sideways and its force will concentrate on joining the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 淮、黃既合，自有控海之勢。

translations.literal: Once Huai and Yellow are joined, they naturally have the force to control the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Huai and Yellow River merge, they will naturally command the estuary.

sentences.zh: 又懼其分而力弱也，必暫塞清江浦河，而嚴司啟閉以防其內奔。

translations.literal: Yet fearing that if divided their force would weaken, one must temporarily block the Qingjiangpu channel and strictly control opening and closing to prevent inward rush.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that division would weaken them, the Qingjiangpu channel must be temporarily blocked, with strict control of sluice gates to prevent water from rushing inland.

sentences.zh: 姑置草灣河，而專復雲梯以還其故道。

translations.literal: For the moment set aside the Caowan channel and concentrate on restoring Yunti to its old course.
translations.idiomatic: For now leave the Caowan channel aside and focus on restoring Yunti to its former course.

sentences.zh: 仍接築淮安新城長堤，以防其末流。

translations.literal: Continue building the long dike at Huai'an Xincheng to guard against the lower current.
translations.idiomatic: Continue the long dike at Huai'an Xincheng to contain the lower reach.

sentences.zh: 使黃、淮力全，涓滴悉趨於海，則力強且專，下流之積沙自去，海不浚而辟，河不挑而深，所謂固堤即以導河，導河即以浚海也。」

translations.literal: If the full force of Yellow and Huai is preserved and every drop rushes to the sea, then the force will be strong and concentrated, accumulated sand in the lower reach will depart of itself, the sea will be cleared without dredging and the river deepened without excavation—this is what is meant by solidifying dikes to guide the river, and guiding the river to dredge the sea."
translations.idiomatic: If the Yellow River and Huai unite their full force and every drop races to the sea, the current will be strong and focused, sand in the lower reach will wash away on its own, the estuary will clear without dredging and the channel deepen without excavation—solidifying dikes guides the river, and guiding the river clears the sea."

sentences.zh: 又言：「黃水入徐，曆邳、宿、桃、清，至清口會淮而東入海。

translations.literal: He further said: "Yellow River water enters Xu, passes through Pi, Su, Tao, and Qing, reaches Qingkou to meet the Huai, and turns east into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Yellow River water enters Xu, runs through Pi, Su, Tao, and Qing, joins the Huai at Qingkou, and turns east to the sea.

sentences.zh: 淮水自洛及鳳，曆盱、泗，至清口會河而東入海。

translations.literal: Huai water from Luo and Feng passes through Xu and Si, reaches Qingkou to meet the river, and turns east into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Huai water from the Luo and Feng regions passes through Xu and Si, meets the Yellow River at Qingkou, and runs east to the sea.

sentences.zh: 此兩河故道也。

translations.literal: These are the old courses of the two rivers.
translations.idiomatic: These are the two rivers' original courses.

sentences.zh: 元漕江南粟，則由揚州直北廟灣入海，未嘗溯淮。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan, grain tribute from Jiangnan was transported straight north from Yangzhou through Miaowan into the sea, never going upstream on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan, Jiangnan grain tribute went straight north from Yangzhou through Miaowan to the sea, never entering the Huai.

sentences.zh: 陳瑄始堤管家諸湖，通淮為運道。

translations.literal: Chen Xuan first diked the Guanjia lakes and opened the Huai as the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuan first diked the Guanjia lakes and linked the Huai as the grain route.

sentences.zh: 慮淮水漲溢，則築高家堰堤以捍之，起武家墩，經大、小澗至阜寧湖，而淮不東侵。

translations.literal: Fearing Huai water would rise and overflow, he built the Gaojia Weir dike to hold it back, starting at Wujiadun, passing through the Great and Small Streams to Funing Lake, so the Huai would not invade eastward.
translations.idiomatic: To hold back rising Huai water, he built the Gaojia Weir from Wujiadun through the Great and Small Streams to Funing Lake, keeping the Huai from spreading east.

sentences.zh: 又慮黃河漲溢，則堤新城北以捍之，起清江浦，沿缽池山、柳浦灣迤東，而黃不南侵。

translations.literal: Also fearing the Yellow River would rise and overflow, he diked the north of Xincheng to hold it back, starting at Qingjiangpu and running east along Bochi Mountain and Liupu Bay, so the Yellow would not invade southward.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yellow River floods as well, he raised dikes north of Xincheng from Qingjiangpu east along Bochi Mountain and Liupu Bay to keep the Yellow from pushing south.

sentences.zh: 其後，堤岸漸傾，水從高堰決入，淮郡遂同魚鱉。

translations.literal: Afterward the dikes gradually collapsed, water broke in through the high weir, and the Huai region became like fish and turtles in water.
translations.idiomatic: Later the dikes gave way, water burst through the high weir, and the Huai region was submerged like a fishpond.

sentences.zh: 而當事者未考其故，謂海口壅閉，宜亟穿支渠。

translations.literal: Yet those in charge did not investigate the cause, saying the river mouth was blocked and branch channels should urgently be cut.
translations.idiomatic: Officials never traced the cause; they blamed a choked estuary and called for urgent cutting of branch channels.

sentences.zh: 詎知草灣一開，西橋以上正河遂至淤阻。

translations.literal: Who would have known that once Caowan was opened, the main channel above Xiqiao would silt up and become blocked?
translations.idiomatic: They did not foresee that opening Caowan would silt up and choke the main channel above Xiqiao.

sentences.zh: 夫新河闊二十餘丈，深僅丈許，較故道僅三十之一，豈能受全河之水？

translations.literal: The new channel is more than twenty zhang wide but only about one zhang deep—barely one thirtieth of the old course—how can it receive the full river's water?
translations.idiomatic: The new channel spans more than twenty zhang but is only about one zhang deep—one thirtieth of the old bed—how could it carry the whole river?

sentences.zh: 下流既壅，上流自潰，此崔鎮諸口所由決也。

translations.literal: When the lower reach is blocked, the upper reach naturally bursts—this is why the openings at Cuizhen and elsewhere broke.
translations.idiomatic: When the lower course chokes, the upper course must break—that is why Cuizhen and the other breaches opened.

sentences.zh: 今新河復塞，故河漸已通流，雖深闊未及原河十一，而兩河全下，沙隨水刷，欲其全復河身不難也。

translations.literal: Now the new channel is blocked again and the old river is gradually flowing once more; though depth and width do not reach one tenth of the original river, with both streams running fully and sand scoured away by the water, restoring the full channel bed is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Now the new channel has silted shut again and the old river is gradually reopening; though it is not yet a tenth of the original depth and width, with both streams running full and sand washing away, restoring the channel is not hard.

sentences.zh: 河身既復，闊者七八里，狹亦不下三四百丈，滔滔東下，何水不容？

translations.literal: Once the channel bed is restored, where it is wide it spans seven or eight li, and even where narrow it is no less than three or four hundred zhang; rushing eastward, what water could it not hold?
translations.idiomatic: Restored, the channel runs seven or eight li wide in places and no less than three or four hundred zhang even at its narrowest; flowing east in full force, what flood could it not carry?

sentences.zh: 匪惟不必別鑿他所，即草灣亦可置勿浚矣。

translations.literal: Not only is there no need to cut elsewhere, even Caowan can be left undredged.
translations.idiomatic: There is no need to cut new channels elsewhere; even Caowan can be left alone.

sentences.zh: 故為今計，惟修復陳瑄故跡，高築南北兩堤，以斷兩河之內灌，則淮、揚昏墊可免。

translations.literal: Therefore for the present plan, only by restoring Chen Xuan's old works, building high dikes on both north and south banks, and cutting off inward flooding from both rivers can the submerged misery of Huai and Yang be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: The present remedy is to restore Chen Xuan's old works, raise high dikes on both banks, and stop inward flooding from both rivers—only then can the Huai-Yang lowlands be saved from inundation.

sentences.zh: 塞黃浦口，築寶應堤，浚東關等淺，修五閘，復五壩，則淮南運道無虞。

translations.literal: Block Huangpukou, build the Baoying dike, dredge the shoals at Dongguan and elsewhere, repair the five sluices, and restore the five dams—then the transport route south of the Huai will be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Seal Huangpukou, build the Baoying dike, dredge shoals such as Dongguan, repair the five sluices, and restore the five dams, and the grain route south of the Huai will be safe.

sentences.zh: 堅塞桃源以下崔鎮口諸決，則全河可歸故道。

translations.literal: Firmly seal the breaches at Cuizhen and elsewhere below Taoyuan, and the whole river can return to its old course.
translations.idiomatic: Seal the breaches at Cuizhen and elsewhere below Taoyuan, and the entire river can return to its old bed.

sentences.zh: 黃、淮既無旁決，並驅入海，則沙隨水刷，海口自復，而桃、清淺阻，又不足言。

translations.literal: Once Yellow and Huai no longer burst sideways but drive together into the sea, sand will be scoured away with the water, the estuary will restore itself, and the shallow obstructions at Tao and Qing are hardly worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Yellow and Huai no longer spill sideways but drive together to the sea, sand will wash away with the current, the estuary will reopen itself, and the shoals at Tao and Qing will hardly matter.

sentences.zh: 此以水治水之法也。

translations.literal: This is the method of using water to govern water.
translations.idiomatic: This is the principle of using water to master water.

sentences.zh: 若夫爬撈之說，僅可行諸閘河，前入屢試無功，徒費工料。」

translations.literal: As for the rake-and-scoop method, it can be used only on canal sluice rivers; predecessors tried it repeatedly without success, wasting labor and materials."
translations.idiomatic: The rake-and-scoop method works only on canal sluices; predecessors tried it repeatedly without success, wasting labor and materials."

sentences.zh: 於是條上六議：曰塞決口以挽正河，曰築堤防以杜潰決，曰復閘壩以防外河，曰創滾水壩以固堤岸，曰止浚海工程以省糜費，曰寢開老黃河之議以仍利涉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted six proposals in order: seal breaches to restore the main channel; build dikes to prevent collapses; restore sluice dams to guard against the outer river; create overflow dams to strengthen the banks; halt estuary dredging works to save wasted expense; and shelve the proposal to open the Old Yellow River so as to preserve ease of crossing.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted six proposals: seal breaches to restore the main channel; build dikes to stop collapses; restore sluice dams against the outer river; create overflow dams to strengthen banks; halt estuary dredging to save expense; and drop the plan to reopen the Old Yellow River so crossings remain easy.

sentences.zh: 帝悉從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor fully granted his requests.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 七年十月，兩河工成，賚季馴、一麟銀幣，而遣給事中尹瑾勘實。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year, work on both rivers was completed; Jixun and Yilin were rewarded with silver and silk, and Supervising Secretary Yin Jin was dispatched to verify the results.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 7, work on both rivers was finished; Jixun and Yilin received silver and silk rewards, and Supervising Secretary Yin Jin was sent to verify the results.

sentences.zh: 八年春進季馴太子太保工部尚書，廕一子。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year Jixun was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Works, and one son received hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 8 Jixun was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Works, and one son received hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 一麟等遷擢有差。

translations.literal: Yilin and others were promoted to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Yilin and others received graded promotions.

sentences.zh: 是役也，築高家堰堤六十餘里，歸仁集堤四十餘里，柳浦灣堤東西七十餘里，塞崔鎮等決口百三十，築徐、睢、邳、宿、桃、清兩岸遙堤五萬六千餘丈，碭、豐大壩各一道，徐、沛、豐、碭縷堤百四十餘里，建崔鎮、徐升、季泰、三義減水石壩四座，遷通濟閘於甘羅城南，淮、揚間堤壩無不修築，費帑金五十六萬有奇。

translations.literal: In this project, more than sixty li of Gaojia Weir dike were built, more than forty li of Guirenji dike, more than seventy li of Liupu Bay dike east and west, one hundred thirty breaches at Cuizhen and elsewhere were sealed, fifty-six thousand-plus zhang of distant dikes were built on both banks at Xu, Sui, Pi, Su, Tao, and Qing, one major dam each at Dang and Feng, more than one hundred forty li of thread dikes at Xu, Pei, Feng, and Dang, four stone overflow dams were built at Cuizhen, Xusheng, Jitai, and Sanyi, the Tongji Sluice was moved south of Ganluo city, and every dike and dam between Huai and Yang was repaired—costing somewhat more than 560,000 taels from the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The project built more than sixty li of Gaojia Weir dike, forty li at Guirenji, seventy li at Liupu Bay, sealed 130 breaches at Cuizhen and elsewhere, raised 56,000-plus zhang of distant dikes on both banks from Xu, Sui, Pi, Su, Tao, and Qing, one major dam each at Dang and Feng, 140 li of thread dikes at Xu, Pei, Feng, and Dang, four stone overflow dams at Cuizhen, Xusheng, Jitai, and Sanyi, moved the Tongji Sluice south of Ganluo city, repaired every dike and dam between Huai and Yang, and cost more than 560,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 其秋擢季馴南京兵部尚書。

translations.literal: That autumn Jixun was promoted to Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Jixun was promoted to Nanjing Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 季馴又請復新集至小浮橋故道，給事中王道成、河南巡撫周鑒等不可而止。

translations.literal: Jixun again requested restoration of the old course from Xinjii to Xiaofuqiao, but Supervising Secretary Wang Daocheng, Henan Grand Coordinator Zhou Jian, and others objected and the plan was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun again asked to restore the old channel from Xinjii to Xiaofuqiao, but Supervising Secretary Wang Daocheng, Henan Grand Coordinator Zhou Jian, and others blocked it.

sentences.zh: 自桂芳、季馴時罷總河不設，其後但以督漕兼理河道。

translations.literal: From the time of Guifang and Jixun the Grand Coordinator for Rivers was abolished and not reinstated; afterward only the grain transport commissioner concurrently managed the river channel.
translations.idiomatic: Since Guifang and Jixun's time the Grand Coordinator for Rivers was abolished; thereafter only the grain transport commissioner also handled river works.

sentences.zh: 高堰初築，清口方暢，流連數年，河道無大患。

translations.literal: When the high weir was first built, Qingkou was still open, and for several years in succession the river channel suffered no major disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When the high weir was first built and Qingkou still ran clear, the channel remained trouble-free for several years.

sentences.zh: 至十五年，封丘、偃師、東明、長垣屢被沖決。

translations.literal: By the fifteenth year, Fengqiu, Yanshi, Dongming, and Changyuan suffered repeated breach disasters.
translations.idiomatic: By year 15, Fengqiu, Yanshi, Dongming, and Changyuan had been breached repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 大學士申時行言：「河所決地在三省，守臣畫地分修，易推委。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing said: "The breach sites lie in three provinces; local officials repair by demarcated territory, which invites buck-passing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing argued: "The breaches lie in three provinces; when local officials repair only their own jurisdictions, responsibility is easily shirked.

sentences.zh: 河道未大壞，不必設都御史，宜遣風力老成給事中一人行河。

translations.literal: The river channel is not yet badly damaged; there is no need to appoint a censor-in-chief—a single seasoned and forceful supervising secretary should be dispatched to inspect the river.
translations.idiomatic: The channel is not yet badly broken; rather than appoint a censor-in-chief, send one seasoned supervising secretary to inspect the river.

sentences.zh: 」乃命工科都給事中常居敬往。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Director of Works Supervising Secretary Chang Jujing was ordered to go.
translations.idiomatic: " Director of Works Supervising Secretary Chang Jujing was dispatched.

sentences.zh: 居敬請修築大社集東至白茅集長堤百里。

translations.literal: Jujing requested construction of a hundred-li long dike from east of Dasheji to Baimaoji.
translations.idiomatic: Jujing proposed a hundred-li long dike from east of Dasheji to Baimaoji.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 初，黃河由徐州小浮橋入運，其河深且近洪，能刷洪以深河，利於運道。

translations.literal: Initially the Yellow River entered the transport channel at Xiaofuqiao in Xuzhou; that channel was deep and close to the Hong rapids, able to scour the Hong shoals and deepen the river—beneficial to the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Yellow River entered the grain route at Xiaofuqiao in Xuzhou; that channel was deep and close to the Hong shoals, scouring them and deepening the bed—a boon to transport.

sentences.zh: 後漸徙沛縣飛雲橋及徐州大、小溜溝。

translations.literal: Later it gradually shifted to Feiyun Bridge in Pei County and the Great and Small Liugou in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later it shifted to Feiyun Bridge in Pei County and the Great and Small Liugou at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 至嘉靖末，決邵家口，出秦溝，由濁河口入運，河淺，迫茶城，茶城歲淤，運道數害。

translations.literal: By the end of Jiajing it breached at Shaojiakou, exited through Qingoukou, entered the transport channel via Zhuohekou; the river grew shallow, pressed on Chacheng, Chacheng silted yearly, and the transport route suffered repeated harm.
translations.idiomatic: By late Jiajing it broke at Shaojiakou, ran out through Qingoukou, and entered the grain route via Zhuohekou; the channel shoaled, pressed on Chacheng, which silted every year, and transport suffered repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年冬，河復南趨，出小浮橋故道，未幾復堙。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Wanli the river again turned south, exiting through the old Xiaofuqiao course, but before long it silted up again.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Wanli 5 the river turned south again through the old Xiaofuqiao bed, but soon silted shut once more.

sentences.zh: 潘季馴之塞崔鎮也，厚築堤岸，束水歸漕。

translations.literal: When Pan Jixun sealed Cuizhen, he built thick dikes and banks to confine the water back into the transport channel.
translations.idiomatic: When Pan Jixun sealed Cuizhen, he built heavy dikes to confine the water back into the grain route.

sentences.zh: 嗣後水發，河臣輒加堤，而河身日高矣。

translations.literal: Afterward, whenever floods came, river officials added to the dikes, and the riverbed grew higher day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever floods rose, river officials piled the dikes higher, and the riverbed rose day by day.

sentences.zh: 於是督漕僉都御史楊一魁欲復黃河故道，請自歸德以下丁家道口浚至石將軍廟，令河仍自小浮橋出。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Censor-in-Chief in charge of grain transport Yang Yikui wished to restore the Yellow River's old course and requested dredging from Dingjiakou below Guide to Shijiangjun Temple so the river would again exit at Xiaofuqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief for grain transport Yang Yikui then sought to restore the Yellow River's old course, proposing dredging from Dingjiakou below Guide to Shijiangjun Temple so the river would again exit at Xiaofuqiao.

sentences.zh: 又言：「善治水者，以疏不以障。

translations.literal: He also said: "Those who govern water well rely on dredging, not on blocking.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Good water management relies on dredging, not on blocking.

sentences.zh: 年來堤上加堤，水高淩空，不啻過顙。

translations.literal: In recent years dikes have been piled on dikes; water looms overhead, no less than above one's forehead.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years dikes have been piled atop dikes until the water looms overhead, higher than a man's brow.

sentences.zh: 濱河城郭，決水可灌。

translations.literal: River-side cities and towns can be flooded by a breach.
translations.idiomatic: Any breach can pour water into cities along the bank.

sentences.zh: 宜測河身深淺，隨處挑浚，而於黃河分流故道，設減水石門以泄暴漲。

translations.literal: The depth of the riverbed should be measured and dredging carried out wherever needed; along the Yellow River's old diversion channels, stone flood gates should be set to discharge sudden floods.
translations.idiomatic: Measure the channel depth and dredge wherever needed; along the Yellow River's old diversion beds, install stone flood gates to release sudden surges.

sentences.zh: 」給事中王士性則請復老黃河故道。

translations.literal: " Supervising Secretary Wang Shixing, for his part, requested restoration of the Old Yellow River course.
translations.idiomatic: " Supervising Secretary Wang Shixing, meanwhile, petitioned to restore the Old Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 大略言：

translations.literal: In general he stated:
translations.idiomatic: In outline he argued:

sentences.zh: 「自徐而下，河身日高，而為堤以束之，堤與徐州城等。

translations.literal: "From Xu downstream the riverbed grows higher daily, yet dikes are built to confine it until the dikes stand level with Xuzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: "Below Xu the riverbed rises daily, yet dikes confine it until they stand level with Xuzhou city.

sentences.zh: 束益急，流益迅，委全力於淮而淮不任。

translations.literal: The tighter the confinement, the swifter the flow; all force is thrown upon the Huai, and the Huai cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The tighter the confinement, the swifter the current; all force is thrown on the Huai, which cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 故昔之黃、淮合，今黃強而淮益縮，不復合矣。

translations.literal: Thus where Yellow and Huai once joined, now the Yellow is strong and the Huai ever more constricted—they no longer meet.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Yellow and Huai once joined, the Yellow has grown strong and the Huai ever more constricted—they no longer merge.

sentences.zh: 黃強而一啟天妃、通濟諸閘，則灌運河如建瓴。

translations.literal: With the Yellow strong, once the Tianfei, Tongji, and other sluices are opened, the transport canal is flooded like water poured from a raised eave.
translations.idiomatic: With the Yellow running strong, opening the Tianfei, Tongji, and other sluices floods the canal like water tipped from a high eave.

sentences.zh: 高、寶一梗，江南之運坐廢。

translations.literal: If Gao and Bao are blocked once, Jiangnan transport is idle and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Block Gao and Bao once, and Jiangnan transport stops cold.

sentences.zh: 淮縮則退而侵泗。

translations.literal: When the Huai is constricted it retreats and invades the Si.
translations.idiomatic: Constricted, the Huai backs up and invades the Si.

sentences.zh: 為祖陵計，不得不建石堤護之。

translations.literal: For the sake of the ancestral tombs, stone dikes must be built to protect them.
translations.idiomatic: To protect the ancestral tombs, stone dikes had to be built.

sentences.zh: 堤增河益高，根本大可虞也。

translations.literal: As dikes rise the river grows higher still—the root of the trouble is deeply worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: As dikes rise, the river rises with them—the root of the danger is grave.

sentences.zh: 河至清河凡四折而後入海。

translations.literal: From the river's reach at Qinghe it turns four times before entering the sea.
translations.idiomatic: From Qinghe the river bends four times before reaching the sea.

sentences.zh: 淮安、高、寶、鹽、興數百萬生靈之命託之一丸泥，決則盡成魚暇矣。

translations.literal: The lives of millions in Huai'an, Gao, Bao, Yan, and Xing rest on a pellet of mud; if it breaks, all become fish and turtles.
translations.idiomatic: Millions in Huai'an, Gao, Bao, Yan, and Xing rest their lives on a pellet of mud; one breach and all become fish in a net.

sentences.zh: 紛紛之議，有欲增堤泗州者，有欲開顏家、灌口、永濟三河，南甃高家堰、北築滾水壩者。

translations.literal: Amid the clamor of proposals, some wished to raise dikes at Sizhou, some to open the three rivers at Yanjia, Guankou, and Yongji, some to face Gaojia Weir with stone to the south and build overflow dams to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Amid competing proposals, some wanted higher dikes at Sizhou, some wanted the Yanjia, Guankou, and Yongji rivers opened, some wanted Gaojia Weir faced with stone to the south and overflow dams built to the north.

sentences.zh: 總不如復河故道，為一勞永逸之計也。

translations.literal: In sum, none compare with restoring the river's old course as a plan for lasting relief from a single effort.
translations.idiomatic: None of these match restoring the old riverbed as a lasting remedy.

sentences.zh: 河故道由三義鎮達葉家沖與淮合，在清河縣北別有濟運河，在縣南蓋支河耳。

translations.literal: The river's old course ran from Sanyizhen to Yejiachong to join the Huai; north of Qinghe County there was a separate canal for grain transport, while south of the county was only a branch channel.
translations.idiomatic: The old course ran from Sanyizhen to Yejiachong to join the Huai; north of Qinghe stood a separate grain canal, while south of the county was only a branch channel.

sentences.zh: 河強奪支河，直趨縣南，而自棄北流之道，然河形固在也。

translations.literal: The river forcibly seized the branch channel and rushed straight south of the county, abandoning its north-flowing course—yet the river's form still remains.
translations.idiomatic: The river seized the branch channel and rushed south of the county, abandoning its north-flowing bed—yet the old channel still survives.

sentences.zh: 自桃源至瓦子灘凡九十里，ＡＨ下不耕，無室廬填墓之礙，雖開河費鉅，而故道一復，為利無窮。」

translations.literal: From Taoyuan to Wazitan is ninety li in all; the low ground is uncultivated, with no dwellings, tombs, or other obstacles. Though opening the channel would cost greatly, once the old course is restored the benefit is endless."
translations.idiomatic: From Taoyuan to Wazitan is ninety li of low, uncultivated ground, free of houses, tombs, or other obstacles. Though the expense would be great, restoring the old course would bring endless benefit."

sentences.zh: 議皆未定。

translations.literal: None of the proposals was settled.
translations.idiomatic: No proposal was finally adopted.

sentences.zh: 居敬及御史喬璧星皆請復專設總理大臣。

translations.literal: Jujing and Censor Qiao Bixing both requested reinstatement of a dedicated supervising minister.
translations.idiomatic: Jujing and Censor Qiao Bixing both asked that a dedicated river commissioner be reinstated.

sentences.zh: 乃命潘季馴為右都御史總督河道。

translations.literal: Pan Jixun was then appointed Right Censor-in-Chief with overall charge of the river channel.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Jixun was appointed Right Censor-in-Chief with overall charge of the river works.

sentences.zh: 時帝從居敬言，罷老黃河議，而季馴抵官，言：「親集故道，故老言『銅幫鐵底』，當開，但歲儉費繁，未能遽行。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor, following Jujing's advice, shelved the Old Yellow River proposal. When Jixun arrived in office he said: "Having personally gathered at the old course, the elders say it has 'copper banks and an iron bottom' and ought to be opened—but famine years make costs heavy, and it cannot be done immediately.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already shelved the Old Yellow River plan on Jujing's advice. On taking office Jixun reported: "I inspected the old bed myself; elders call it 'copper banks and an iron bottom' and say it should be opened—but famine makes costs heavy, and it cannot be done at once.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「黃水濁而強，汶、泗清且弱，交會茶城。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Yellow water is muddy and strong; Wen and Si water is clear and weak; they meet at Chacheng.
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "Yellow water is muddy and strong, Wen and Si water clear and weak; they meet at Chacheng.

sentences.zh: 伏秋黃水發，則倒灌人漕，沙停而淤，勢所必至。

translations.literal: When Yellow water rises in the summer and autumn slack season, it backflows into the transport channel; sand settles and silts up—this is necessarily so.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow rises in the flood season, it backflows into the grain route; sand settles and silts up—inevitably so.

sentences.zh: 然黃水一落，漕即從之，沙隨水去，不浚自通，縱有淺阻，不過旬日。

translations.literal: Yet once Yellow water falls, the transport channel follows it; sand goes with the water and clears without dredging—even if there are shallow obstructions, they last no more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once the Yellow falls, the grain route follows; sand washes away without dredging—even shoals clear within ten days.

sentences.zh: 往時建古洪、內華二閘，黃漲則閉閘以遏濁流，黃退則啟閘以縱泉水。

translations.literal: In former times the Guhong and Neihua sluices were built; when the Yellow rose the sluices were closed to block muddy flow, and when the Yellow receded they were opened to release spring water.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Guhong and Neihua sluices were built: when the Yellow rose, the gates closed to block muddy flow; when it fell, they opened to release clear spring water.

sentences.zh: 近者居敬復增建鎮口閘，去河愈近，則吐納愈易。

translations.literal: Recently Jujing additionally built the Zhenkou Sluice; the closer to the river, the easier intake and discharge.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Jujing added the Zhenkou Sluice; placed closer to the river, it regulates flow more easily.

sentences.zh: 但當嚴閘禁如清江浦三閘之法，則河渠永賴矣。

translations.literal: One need only enforce sluice control as strictly as the three sluices at Qingjiangpu, and the river and canal will forever depend on this.
translations.idiomatic: Enforce sluice control as strictly as at Qingjiangpu's three gates, and the river and canal will be secure for good.

sentences.zh: 」帝方委季馴，即從其言，罷故道之議。

translations.literal: " The emperor, having just entrusted Jixun, immediately followed his words and shelved the old-course proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, having just entrusted Jixun, accepted his view and dropped the old-course plan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，水患益甚。

translations.literal: Before long, flood disasters grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Before long floods grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月，黃水暴漲，決獸醫口月堤，漫李景高口新堤，沖入夏鎮內河，壞田廬，沒人民無算。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year Yellow water surged violently, breached the crescent dike at Shouyikou, overflowed the new dike at Lijinggaokou, rushed into the inner river at Xiazhen, destroyed fields and dwellings, and drowned people beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 17 the Yellow surged violently, broke the crescent dike at Shouyikou, overtopped the new dike at Lijinggaokou, poured into Xiazhen's inner river, destroyed fields and homes, and drowned countless people.

sentences.zh: 十月，決口塞。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the breach was sealed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the breach was sealed.

sentences.zh: 十八年，大溢，徐州水積城中者逾年。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year there was a great flood; water standing in Xuzhou city lasted more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 a great flood left water standing in Xuzhou city for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 眾議遷城改河。

translations.literal: Many debated relocating the city and changing the river's course.
translations.idiomatic: Many proposed relocating the city and changing the river's course.

sentences.zh: 季馴浚魁山支河以通之，起蘇伯湖至小河口，積水乃消。

translations.literal: Jixun dredged the Kuishan branch channel to release it, from Subo Lake to Xiaohekou, and the standing water then subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun dredged the Kuishan branch from Subo Lake to Xiaohekou to drain the flood, and the standing water finally receded.

sentences.zh: 十九年九月，泗州大水，州治淹三尺，居民沉溺十九，浸及祖陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the nineteenth year Sizhou suffered great flood; water in the prefectural seat stood three chi deep, nine tenths of residents were drowned, and the flood reached the ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 19 Sizhou flooded; water in the prefectural seat stood three chi deep, nine tenths of residents were drowned, and the flood reached the ancestral tombs.

sentences.zh: 而山陽復河決，江都、邵伯又因湖水下注，田廬浸傷。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shanyang again suffered a river breach, and in Jiangdu and Shaobo lake water poured down and damaged fields and dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Shanyang broke again, and in Jiangdu and Shaobo lake water poured down and damaged fields and homes.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書曾同亨上其事，議者紛起。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zeng Tongheng reported the matter, and debaters arose in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zeng Tongheng reported the disaster, and debate erupted on all sides.

sentences.zh: 乃命工科給事中張貞觀往泗州勘視水勢，而從給事中楊其休言，放季馴歸，用舒應龍為工部尚書總督河道。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary of Works Zhang Zhenguan was ordered to go to Sizhou to inspect water conditions; following Supervising Secretary Yang Qixiu's advice, Jixun was released to return home and Shu Yinglong was appointed Minister of Works with overall charge of the river channel.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary of Works Zhang Zhenguan was sent to inspect Sizhou; on Supervising Secretary Yang Qixiu's advice, Jixun was dismissed and Shu Yinglong appointed Minister of Works with overall charge of river works.

sentences.zh: 二十年三月，季馴將去，條上辨惑者六事，力言河不兩行，新河不當開，支渠不當浚。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year, as Jixun was about to leave, he submitted six items clarifying misconceptions, forcefully stating that the river cannot run in two courses, new channels should not be opened, and branch channels should not be dredged.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 20, as Jixun prepared to leave, he submitted six clarifications, insisting that the river cannot run in two courses, new channels should not be opened, and branch channels should not be dredged.

sentences.zh: 又著書曰河防一覽，大旨在築堤障河，束水歸漕；

translations.literal: He also wrote a book called Overview of River Defense, whose main point was to build dikes to block the river and confine water back into the transport channel;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Overview of River Defense, arguing chiefly for dikes to block the river and confine water to the grain route;

sentences.zh: 築堰障淮，逼淮注黃。

translations.literal: build weirs to block the Huai and force Huai water into the Yellow;
translations.idiomatic: weirs to block the Huai and force it into the Yellow;

sentences.zh: 以清刷濁，沙隨水去。

translations.literal: use clear water to scour muddy water, and sand departs with the water.
translations.idiomatic: use clear water to scour muddy water so sand washes away with the current.

sentences.zh: 合則流急，急則蕩滌而河深；

translations.literal: When joined the flow is swift; when swift it scours and the river grows deep;
translations.idiomatic: United, the current runs swift; swift, it scours and the channel deepens;

sentences.zh: 分則流緩，緩則停滯而沙積。

translations.literal: when divided the flow is slow; when slow it stagnates and sand accumulates.
translations.idiomatic: divided, it slackens; slack, it stagnates and sand piles up.

sentences.zh: 上流既急，則海口自辟而無待於開。

translations.literal: When the upper reach is swift, the estuary opens itself without need of excavation.
translations.idiomatic: When the upper reach runs swift, the estuary opens itself without dredging.

sentences.zh: 其治堤之法，有縷堤以束其流，有遙堤以寬其勢，有滾水壩以泄其怒。

translations.literal: His methods for managing dikes included thread dikes to confine the flow, distant dikes to widen its force, and overflow dams to release its fury.
translations.idiomatic: His dike methods included thread dikes to confine flow, distant dikes to widen its force, and overflow dams to release surges.

sentences.zh: 法甚詳，言甚辯。

translations.literal: The methods were very detailed and the argument very eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: The methods were detailed and the argument eloquent.

sentences.zh: 然當是時，水勢橫潰，徐、泗、淮、揚間無歲不受患，祖陵被水。

translations.literal: Yet at that time water burst in all directions; between Xu, Si, Huai, and Yang no year passed without disaster, and the ancestral tombs were flooded.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at that time water burst everywhere; between Xu, Si, Huai, and Yang no year passed without disaster, and the ancestral tombs were flooded.

sentences.zh: 季馴謂當自消，已而不驗。

translations.literal: Jixun said it would subside of itself, but this was not borne out.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun said the flood would subside on its own, but it did not.

sentences.zh: 於是季馴言詘，而分黃導淮之議由此起矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jixun's argument was defeated, and from this arose the proposal to divide the Yellow and guide the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun's argument failed, and from this arose the proposal to split the Yellow and guide the Huai.

sentences.zh: 貞觀抵泗州言：「臣謁祖陵，見泗城如水上浮盂，盂中之水復滿。

translations.literal: Zhenguan, arriving at Sizhou, said: "When I visited the ancestral tombs, I saw Sizhou city like a floating bowl on water, and the water inside the bowl was full again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan reported from Sizhou: "When I visited the ancestral tombs, Sizhou city looked like a bowl floating on water, and the bowl was full again.

sentences.zh: 祖陵自神路至三橋、丹墀，無一不被水。

translations.literal: From the spirit path to the three bridges and the red steps at the ancestral tombs, nothing was untouched by water.
translations.idiomatic: From the spirit path to the three bridges and the red steps, nothing at the tombs was dry.

sentences.zh: 且高堰危如累卵，又高、寶隱禍也。

translations.literal: Moreover the high weir is precarious as piled eggs, and Gao and Bao conceal disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The high weir stands precarious as piled eggs, and Gao and Bao hide disaster in waiting.

sentences.zh: 今欲泄淮，當以辟海口積沙為第一義。

translations.literal: Now if one wishes to discharge the Huai, clearing accumulated sand at the estuary must be the first priority.
translations.idiomatic: To release the Huai, clearing accumulated estuary sand must come first.

sentences.zh: 然泄淮不若殺黃，而殺黃於淮流之既合，不若殺於未合。

translations.literal: Yet discharging the Huai is inferior to reducing the Yellow; and reducing the Yellow after Huai and Yellow have joined is inferior to reducing it before they join.
translations.idiomatic: Yet releasing the Huai is less effective than weakening the Yellow; and weakening the Yellow after the two rivers join is less effective than doing so before they meet.

sentences.zh: 但殺於既合者與運無妨，殺於未合者與運稍礙。

translations.literal: But reducing it after they have joined does not hinder transport, while reducing it before they join slightly obstructs transport.
translations.idiomatic: Weakening the Yellow after the rivers join does not hinder transport; doing so before they meet slightly obstructs it.

sentences.zh: 別標本，究利害，必當殺於未合之先。

translations.literal: Distinguishing root from branch and weighing benefit against harm, one must reduce the Yellow before they join.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing root against branch and benefit against harm, the Yellow must be weakened before the rivers meet.

sentences.zh: 至於廣入海之途，則自鮑家口、黃家營至魚溝、金城左右，地勢頗下，似當因而利導之。

translations.literal: As for widening the route to the sea, from Baojiakou and Huangjiaying to the vicinity of Yugou and Jincheng, the terrain is rather low; it seems one ought to take advantage of this and lead the water beneficially.
translations.idiomatic: To widen the path to the sea, the stretch from Baojiakou and Huangjiaying to Yugou and Jincheng lies at relatively low elevation; the sensible course is to follow the land and guide the current accordingly.

sentences.zh: 」貞觀又會應龍及總漕陳於陛等言：「淮、黃同趨者惟海，而淮之由黃達海者惟清口。

translations.literal: Zhenguan further joined with Yinglong and the Grand Canal Commissioner Chen Yubi and others in stating: "The Huai and Yellow Rivers converge only at the sea, and the Huai reaches the sea by way of the Yellow only through Qingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhenguan then met with Shu Yinglong, Grand Canal Commissioner Chen Yubi, and others, who argued: "The Huai and the Yellow meet the sea only together, and the Huai reaches the sea via the Yellow solely through Qingkou.

sentences.zh: 自海沙開浚無期，因而河身日高；

translations.literal: Because dredging the estuarine sand has no prospect of completion, the riverbed daily grows higher;
translations.idiomatic: With no end in sight to dredging the sand at the estuary, the river channel rose day by day;

sentences.zh: 自河流倒灌無已，因而清口日塞。

translations.literal: Because the river's backflow is unending, Qingkou daily grows more blocked.
translations.idiomatic: and with the river's reverse flow never ceasing, Qingkou silted up further each day.

sentences.zh: 以致淮水上浸祖陵，漫及高、寶，而興、泰運堤亦沖決矣。

translations.literal: With the result that Huai water rose to inundate the ancestral tombs, spread as far as Gaoyou and Baoying, and the transport dikes at Xinghua and Taizhou were also breached.
translations.idiomatic: The consequence was that Huai water backed up into the imperial ancestral tombs, spread through Gaoyou and Baoying, and breached the transport dikes at Xinghua and Taizhou as well.

sentences.zh: 今議辟清口沙，且分黃河之流於清口上流十里地，去口不遠，不至為運道梗。

translations.literal: Now it is proposed to clear the sand at Qingkou and additionally to divide the Yellow River's flow ten li above Qingkou—not far from the mouth, so as not to obstruct the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: The present plan is to dredge the sand bar at Qingkou and divert part of the Yellow River ten li upstream of the mouth—close enough not to choke the grain route.

sentences.zh: 分於上，復合於下，則沖海之力專。

translations.literal: Split above and reunited below, the force driving toward the sea would be concentrated.
translations.idiomatic: If the stream is divided above and reunited below, the force scouring toward the sea will be concentrated.

sentences.zh: 合必於草灣之下，恐其復沖正河，為淮城患也。

translations.literal: The reunion must be below Caowan, lest it again scour the main channel and become a hazard to Huai'an city.
translations.idiomatic: The reunion must occur downstream of Caowan, lest the current swing back into the main channel and threaten Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 塞鮑家口、黃家營二決，恐橫沖新河，散溢無歸。

translations.literal: Closing the breaches at Baojiakou and Huangjiaying risks a lateral assault on the new channel, with water spilling in all directions and nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Sealing the breaks at Baojiakou and Huangjiaying risks a sideways rush into the new channel, with water spreading everywhere and no outlet.

sentences.zh: 兩岸俱堤，則東北清沭、海安窪下地不虞潰決。

translations.literal: Dikes on both banks would ensure that the low-lying ground of Qingmiao and Hai'an to the northeast need not fear collapse.
translations.idiomatic: With dikes on both banks, the low ground of Qingmiao and Hai'an to the northeast would no longer be at risk of breach.

sentences.zh: 計費凡三十六萬有奇。

translations.literal: The estimated cost totals somewhat more than 360,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: The projected expense came to a little over 360,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 若海口之塞，則潮汐莫窺其涯，難施畚鍤。

translations.literal: As for the blocked estuary, the tides conceal its limits and shovel work cannot be deployed.
translations.idiomatic: As for the choked estuary, the tides hide its bounds and no shovel work can be applied.

sentences.zh: 惟淮、黃合流東下，河身滌而漸深，海口刷而漸辟，亦事理之可必者。

translations.literal: Only when the Huai and Yellow unite and flow eastward will the riverbed be scoured and gradually deepen, the estuary be flushed and gradually open—a course of things necessarily to be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the Huai and Yellow join and run east together will the channel be scoured deeper and the estuary flushed open—a result that reason itself demands.

sentences.zh: 」帝悉從其請。

translations.literal: The Emperor fully granted their request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved their proposals in full.

sentences.zh: 乃議於清口上流北岸，開腰鋪支河達於草灣。

translations.literal: They then proposed opening the Yaopu branch canal on the north bank upstream of Qingkou, reaching Caowan.
translations.idiomatic: Officials then proposed cutting the Yaopu branch canal on the north bank upstream of Qingkou, running it to Caowan.

sentences.zh: 既而淮水自決張福堤。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the Huai broke through the Zhangfu Embankment of its own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Huai burst the Zhangfu Embankment on its own.

sentences.zh: 直隸巡按彭應參言：「祖陵度可無虞，且方東備倭警，宜暫停河工。
